Assess Simulations

Source: R/spatial_prediction.R
assess_simulation.Rd

Evaluates models using joint data and surface simulations.

Usage

assess_simulation(
  obj_sim,
  models,
  control_mcmc = set_control_mcmc(),
  seed = NULL,
  spatial_scale,
  messages = getOption("RiskMap.messages", TRUE),
  target = identity,
  area_summary = NULL,
  boundaries = NULL,
  col_names = NULL,
  pred_objective = c("mse", "classify"),
  categories = NULL
)

Arguments

obj_sim

Output from simulate_glgpm() with both data and surface, from a generating model without grouped re() effects. The generating model can have any link.

models

A named list of fitted models returned by glgpm() or model specifications returned by specify_glgpm(). Each object defines a candidate model specification and is refitted to every simulated dataset; its estimated parameter values are not reused.

control_mcmc

A control object for MCMC sampling, created with set_control_mcmc(). Default is set_control_mcmc().

seed

Optional non-negative integer that makes the assessment reproducible; see Details. The caller's random number state is restored on exit. When NULL (the default), the seeds of the simulations are drawn from the session's random number generator.

spatial_scale

The scale(s) at which predictions are assessed: "grid", "area", or c("grid", "area") to compute both from a single fit-and-predict pass over the simulations.

messages

Logical, whether to report on the assessment, with a progress bar as described in riskmap_progress. Defaults to the option RiskMap.messages, or TRUE if it is not set.

target

A function that converts a numeric matrix of means to a numeric matrix of the scientific target, with the same dimensions. The mean is the probability for a binomial model, the mean per unit exposure for a Poisson model and the value itself for a Gaussian model. The default, identity(), scores the mean itself, such as prevalence. Other targets are functions of the mean, such as qlogis() to score prevalence on the logit scale, or function(mu) pnorm((-2 - mu) / sd) for the proportion of children stunted from a Gaussian model of height-for-age z-scores with residual standard deviation sd. See Details.

area_summary

A function that combines a numeric vector of grid-cell targets within one area and returns one finite numeric value, such as base::mean() or base::sum(). Required only when spatial_scale includes "area".

boundaries

An sf object containing only POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON geometries, required if spatial_scale includes "area".

col_names

Column name in boundaries containing unique region names. If NULL, defaults to "region".

pred_objective

A character vector specifying objectives, either "mse", "classify", or both.

categories

A numeric vector of thresholds defining categories for classification. Required if pred_objective = "classify".

Value

A list of class RiskMap_assess_simulation:

pred_objective

One element per requested spatial_scale ("grid" and/or "area"), each holding mse, a matrix with one row per model and one column per simulation, and/or classify, the classification metrics of each model and simulation.

fits

A data frame with one row per model and simulation, giving the status of the fit ("ok" or "failed"), the error message of a failed fit and any warnings.

estimates

A list with, for each model, a matrix of the parameter estimates, one row per simulation.

n_sim, spatial_scale

The number of simulations and the spatial scales assessed.

Details

Every model is scored on the scale of the mean, each through its own inverse link, so the links of the generating model and of the candidates need not agree. The true target at each grid location is target() applied to the simulated mean, which is the generating model's inverse link of the simulated linear predictor. That linear predictor includes the covariates, any offset and, when the generating model has one, the realised nugget. Each candidate is refitted to every simulated dataset, its predictive draws of the linear predictor are mapped to the mean through the inverse link of the refitted model, and target() is then applied to those draws. A probit candidate on simulations from a logit model is thus scored on the same prevalence as the truth. Candidates predict with their own covariates and offset, and those with a nugget include it in their predictions when the generating model has one.

The target receives the mean rather than the linear predictor, which is what the transform argument of predict.RiskMap() receives, because models with different links share no linear-predictor scale. Every link is monotone, so a target defined on the linear predictor of a given link can be written as a function of the mean, as qlogis() gives the logit scale.

The target of an area is area_summary() applied to the targets at the grid locations that fall within it, with equal weight, unlike the exact fractional coverage used by predict.RiskMap() with boundaries. Areas without grid locations are left out of the area-level assessment, with a warning. Predictive draws are joint within each area, which is all that area-level targets need.

Each simulation has its own seed, derived from seed or, without one, from the current random number generator state, and shared by all models so that their fits and predictions use common random numbers. A fit or prediction that fails does not stop the assessment: its results are missing, and the failure is recorded in fits and reported in a warning, as are warnings from the fits.

Examples

library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE
data(italy_sim)
italy_subset <- italy_sim[1:30, ]
italy_grid <- italy_subset[!duplicated(st_coordinates(italy_subset)), ]
model <- specify_glgpm(
  y ~ pop_dens + gp(), italy_subset, family = "gaussian",
  parameters = list(beta = c(1, 0.001), sigma2 = 1, phi = 20,
                    sigma2_me = 0.1)
)
simulations <- simulate_glgpm(
  model, nsim = 1, what = c("data", "surface"),
  prediction_grid = italy_grid, seed = 1
)
boundary <- st_sf(
  region = "study_area",
  geometry = st_convex_hull(st_union(italy_grid))
)
assessment <- assess_simulation(
  simulations,
  models = list(candidate = model),
  spatial_scale = c("grid", "area"),
  area_summary = mean,
  boundaries = boundary,
  pred_objective = "mse",
  messages = FALSE
)
